root_cause.text: A lock inversion deadlock occurs in `fs/ntfs3` because `ntfs_read_folio()` acquires the inode mutex (`ni_lock`) before `ni_read_folio_cmpr()` attempts to lock other pages in a compressed frame, violating the standard VFS lock ordering of Page Lock -> `ni_lock`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the removal of `ni_lock(ni)` and `ni_unlock(ni)` from `ntfs_read_folio()` in `fs/ntfs3/inode.c`, and instead places them inside `ni_read_folio_cmpr()` in `fs/ntfs3/frecord.c` after the page locks are acquired. This is supported by the commit message: "This is caused by a lock inversion deadlock involving the inode mutex (ni_lock) and page locks... Instead, acquire ni_lock inside ni_read_folio_cmpr() ONLY AFTER all required page locks for the frame have been successfully acquired."

bic_trace_step.reason: In `ntfs_readpage` (lines 485-509), when the inode is compressed, the code acquires the inode lock `ni_lock(ni)` on line 503 while already holding the lock for the current page (which was locked by the VFS before calling `ntfs_readpage`). Inside `ni_readpage_cmpr(ni, page)`, the code will attempt to lock other pages in the compressed frame. This creates a lock inversion deadlock because it mixes the lock order: Page Lock -> `ni_lock` (for the first page) and `ni_lock` -> Page Lock (for subsequent pages in the compressed frame).
